Recently, I was approached by a private collector who had noticed I'm a mod on a few comic book subverses. He asked if I would be interested in taking some cash in exchange for putting up a small blurb and contact info for anyone wanting to sell off their older comic books. I told him I didn't know if that would go over well with the subverses but that I would think about it-- and post about it in those respective subs to get their thoughts.

Then, I was approached by an indie comic book creator who wanted to know if I'd take cash for putting up the cover of their comic book in the sidebar of /v/comicbooks. I basically told him the same thing.

Anyways, this led to a discussion on the possibility of starting an advertising network on Voat with a marketing friend of mine and some others. The jist of our idea was, the ads would be static and "non-distracting" (re: unanimated) located in the sidebar. There would also be a limit to how much advertised content there could be. Ads would also be limited to the sidebar and clearly labelled, so none of that "native advertising" bullshit, or stickies, or ads disguised as posts.

We also wanted to stay far away from peripheral advertising. Basically, the subject of ads would have to be exclusively tailored to the subverse, and they should have a personal touch. So, ads like for the private collector and the indie guy would be accepted, but ads for, say, Disney's The Littlest Mermaid or Best Buy's sale on Deadpool plushies wouldn't be allowed in /v/Marvel.

The hope would be to grow the network of available subverses to advertise on. Right now, the thinking is that the profits would be split 50%-50% between whoever's taking care of the backend (finding people who want to advertise, processing payments) and whoever the point of contact is for the subverse that is being advertised on.

I tried the layout here a couple days ago, and most of the ads end up looking more like those old school ads from a newspaper classified section. You can see what it would look like for yourself, now, in /v/asdf.

Anyways, I was interested in your thoughts on the matter. Yes, 'your' as in 'you' as in 'the person who randomly clicked on this post after it popped up in their front or /v/all feeds'. It's just an idea that's being kicked around. And like I said, I'd still have to run it by the subscribers in my other subs.
